Oct 20, 2026

## **Fast Finality \+ Networking**

Invited [francesco.damato@ethereum.org](mailto:francesco.damato@ethereum.org) [Sukun Tarachandani](mailto:sukun.tarachandani@ethereum.org) [raul.kripalani@ethereum.org](mailto:raul.kripalani@ethereum.org) [Roberto Saltini](mailto:roberto.saltini@ethereum.org) [Yann Vonlanthen](mailto:yann.vonlanthen@ethereum.org) [Kamil Salakhiev](mailto:kamil.salakhiev@ethereum.org) [francesco@ethlabs.org](mailto:francesco@ethlabs.org) [anton.nashatyrev@consensys.com](mailto:anton.nashatyrev@consensys.com) [mikhail.kalinin@consensys.com](mailto:mikhail.kalinin@consensys.com) [barnabe@ethlabs.org](mailto:barnabe@ethlabs.org) [ttsao@offchainlabs.com](mailto:ttsao@offchainlabs.com) [Csaba Kiraly](mailto:csaba.kiraly@ethereum.org) [Kevaundray Wedderburn](mailto:kevaundray.wedderburn@ethereum.org) ~~[Ben Edgington](mailto:ben.edgington@ethereum.org)~~

Attachments [Fast Finality + Networking](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/event?eid=M2xrYm12c2Y2cThqbXBodW5pc200ZzF1bXNfMjAyNjEwMjBUMTEwMDAwWiBzdWt1bi50YXJhY2hhbmRhbmlAZXRoZXJldW0ub3Jn)

Meeting records [Transcript](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Z_drNyny_dr_DxNLnE90qYknn8Lqz66OF8WeGbN0oO0/edit?usp=drive_web&tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex) 

### **Summary**

Sync call debated post-quantum networking and decoupled consensus, prioritizing incremental finality improvements.

**Post Quantum Network Scope**  
Participants discussed balancing post-quantum design integration with conservative scoping and development timelines.

**Decoupled Consensus Mechanics**  
Attendees debated slot and sub-round decoupling alongside committee rotation and attestation propagation timings.

**Minimal Viable Approach**  
The group agreed to target a minimal viable decoupled consensus focusing on delivering measurable finality improvements.

### **Decisions**

## Needs Further Discussion

* **Committee staggering and sub-round structure** The group actively deliberated committee staggering and sub-round structures, leaving final implementation and mechanics open for further evaluation.

* **Postponing Staggered Publishing Subround Discussions** The participants agreed to defer the detailed discussion on staggered publishing and subround committee structures to a separate upcoming call.

## Aligned

* **Baseline AR design delivery prioritization** The participants agreed to deliver the baseline AR design first and defer post-quantum networking considerations.

* **Protocol specification without explicit slot coupling** Participants agreed to design the protocol specification without explicit slot coupling while allowing implicit coupling in practice.

* **Adopting Minimal Viable Decoupled Consensus** The team aligned on adopting a minimal viable decoupled consensus approach for AR to deliver improved finality while punting reward fairness and complex trade-offs to the future.

### **Next steps**

- [ ] \[Yann Vonlanthen\] Invite Developers: Invite lean client developers to the call and share the meeting information in the FF group.

- [ ] \[Sukun Tarachandani\] Discuss EIP Implementation: Discuss the EIP implementation with Loadar to encourage them to adopt the changes.

- [ ] \[Sukun Tarachandani\] Present Benchmarks: Present DevNet benchmark results to Loadar to demonstrate the benefits of the proposed networking changes before the next DevNet week.

- [ ] \[The group\] Present PQ Timelines: Present models and timelines related to Post Quantum transitions.

- [ ] \[Yann Vonlanthen\] Schedule Meeting: Organize the next meeting for next week to continue the discussion.

- [ ] \[The group\] Define Parameters: Specify the sub round timing and operational parameters for the protocol.

### **Details**

**Meeting Cadence and Agenda Scope Expansion**: Yann Vonlanthen proposed changing the consensus and networking sync call from bi-weekly to weekly, alternating between post-quantum networking and non-post-quantum networking, and broadening participation by inviting lean client developers ([00:00:24](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.wtskcd1bpp8h)). Roberto Saltini questioned whether a fixed split between post-quantum and non-post-quantum topics was helpful given their deep interrelation, suggesting flexibility instead ([00:04:02](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.musisez7hf51)). Kevaundray Wedderburn noted that lean clients would initially observe for prototyping and benchmarking, and suggested prioritizing star networking while treating post-quantum networking as a separate challenge ([00:05:20](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.7qqqln66xjyg)).

---

**Post-Quantum Networking Scope and Design Timing**: Sukun Tarachandani raised concerns that designing with post-quantum networking in mind would significantly increase scope, noting they are targeting a conservative 8-slot round and that post-quantum slot structures require two rounds of aggregations. Yann Vonlanthen suggested de-risking by adopting post-quantum compatible design choices early, such as accepting large bit lists rather than minimizing size ([00:06:49](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.pfvveltqwjsl)). Barnabé Monnot recommended developing a strong estimate of naive post-quantum networking and finality timelines as input for Devcon. Csaba Kiraly advised separating generic networking research (message sizes, traffic patterns) from specific design choices, recommending collection of post-quantum information without locking in premature design decisions ([00:08:19](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.22lbdf971iri)).

---

**Attestation Scheduling and Incentive Impacts**: Yann Vonlanthen introduced a consensus scheduling proposal where validators send FFG votes at round start and networking resolves the scheduling, noting this could impact fairness by allowing large entities to schedule all attestations in their proposals for higher rewards. Mikhail questioned whether post-quantum changes these incentive implications, while Kamil Salakhiev noted that a baseline model with roughly 16 attesters per subnet helps distribute traffic and prevent traffic bursts ([00:12:44](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.l1ajbgqh2c9v)).

---

**Slow-Path and Fast-Path Pipeline Design**: Kamil Salakhiev and Csaba Kiraly outlined a post-quantum pipeline comprising signature propagation, aggregation, and final aggregate propagation ([00:16:57](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.jozrj0rib17w)) ([00:20:21](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.duaowam3yg8j)). Kamil Salakhiev noted that powerful actors like Binance might provide hardware for rapid aggregation to improve user experience, while Csaba Kiraly distinguished between a slow-path standard protocol and a fast-path standardizing self-interested actions by powerful actors ([00:18:32](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.97oqlka2hg0f)).

---

**Decoupled Consensus for Attestation Aggregation and Client Implementation Challenges**: Sukun Tarachandani asked what level of detail is needed to propose decoupled consensus for attestation aggregation, prompting Ben Edgington to advise delivering attestation aggregation first and addressing post-quantum later based on the software development principle of not needing it yet ([00:22:04](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.wq4uytlygthl)). Sukun Tarachandani stated that advanced techniques like topic-layer prioritization face implementation resistance because clients will not adopt them without strict EIP mandates ([00:25:22](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.tir9rhrftx91)). Mikhail proposed a backward-compatible gossip subtopic for bundled attestations, but Sukun Tarachandani noted that while Prysm and Lighthouse agreed to implement proposed EIPs, clients like Teku and Lodestar resisted unless absolutely necessary ([00:26:58](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.ybzs3cbn2bu)).

---

**Client Benchmarks and Push for Adoption**: Yann Vonlanthen suggested showcasing DevNet benchmarks before Algorand DevNet week to demonstrate how attestation aggregation helps and to push client adoption ([00:28:23](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.anlo4x5p84un)). Sukun Tarachandani noted they shared Cambridge workshop slides with Lodestar, whose primary pushback concerned compatibility with post-quantum requirements ([00:29:53](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.8c6nl2wddyxc)).

---

**Agile Development and Baseline Design for Attestation Aggregation**: Ben Edgington and Yann Vonlanthen discussed whether to include properties like self-selection or slow rotation from day one or adopt an agile approach starting with a basic design. Ben Edgington initially favored starting with something basic, but noted that if committee rotation is justified, it should be included from day one ([00:31:27](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.qxpg6ir8rzsw)).

---

**Committee Rotation and Staggered Versus Multiple Committees**: Sukun Tarachandani and Yann Vonlanthen debated whether to use multiple committees or stagger a single committee across the slot. Yann Vonlanthen advocated for the staggered approach to decouple rounds from slots, whereas Sukun Tarachandani expressed a preference for multiple committees on the same subnet design ([00:32:48](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.rvle0hjuukxo)).

---

**Bandwidth Efficiency and Aggregate Deadlines**: Csaba Kiraly argued in favor of larger aggregates with aggregate deadlines rather than small committees with short deadlines to improve bandwidth utilization and resilience against network fluctuations and subnet bandwidth limits. Yann Vonlanthen expressed full agreement with this intuition, noting it supports staggered committees over single-committee slots ([00:36:42](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.45tf3kcxhq0l)).

![][image1]

---

**Sub-Round Mechanics and Rewards Fairness**: Mikhail explained that peer-to-peer operations will use sub-rounds instead of slots and that reward and penalty fairness requires including sub-round numbers in attestations and signing over them ([00:38:31](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.enxrdbucbjmw)). Csaba Kiraly and Roberto Saltini sought clarification on sub-round boundaries and whether sub-rounds timeout when jobs are finished or hit a time limit ([00:40:10](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.8dkdzy33dxdj)).

![][image2]

---

**Sub-Round and Slot Decoupling Challenges**: Yann Vonlanthen contrasted an approach where sub-rounds always match slot lengths with one where sub-rounds operate on independent timelines across slots ([00:44:08](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.5anrfkn66lvp)) ([00:54:44](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.u74xy0ijdh07)). Mikhail noted that fully decoupling sub-rounds from slots introduces unknowns regarding proposer fairness and discouragement attacks, suggesting they start with one committee per sub-round per subnet and add staggering if necessary ([00:51:23](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.x9aul0xstkuq)).

---

**Practical Coupling of Sub-Rounds to Block Cadence**: Ben Edgington concluded that while protocol specifications can remain uncoupled from slot times for purist reasons, practical deployments will likely remain implicitly coupled to block publication cadences because blocks serve as the message carriers ([00:57:07](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.3lqu5qdi2jb8)). Mikhail agreed, adding that future reductions in slot time will require adjusting peer-to-peer layers for the finality gadget if slots and sub-rounds remain coupled ([00:58:32](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.u376ley4exng)).

---

**Decoupling Slots and Finality Cadence**: Mikhail and Ben Edgington discussed adjusting the time and number of sub-rounds, noting they could be fully decoupled with the necessary methods and parameters. Ben Edgington argued that full decoupling requires two trade-offs: sacrificing reward fairness and committing fully to traffic prioritization so time-bound events take priority while regular traffic runs in the background ([00:59:55](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.hs04zz9f7w4f)). Yann Vonlanthen expressed surprise, noting their concern about downstream effects on finality time whenever slot length changes ([01:01:11](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.ve3jo8l6qakd)). Barnabé Monnot added that post-quantum transitions make decoupling the right choice since slot decreases will likely be less frequent than post-quantum transitions. Roberto Saltini agreed that network prioritization is a prerequisite for this approach ([01:02:33](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.9nh1l0n2w24q)). Ben Edgington suggested punting difficult questions like reward fairness and power-of-two slot counts to the future, recommending that they decouple in protocol for AR while keeping the round constant tied to current slot times to bypass difficult immediate questions ([01:04:11](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.m4w3maot6o1v)). Roberto Saltini raised concerns about overlapping transmissions like station and goldfish votes, but Ben Edgington noted they would ensure current designs do not conflict while leaving the machinery in place for future adjustments ([01:05:13](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.5r9t3vgl1635)).

---

**Attestation Propagation and Aggregation Timing**: Yann Vonlanthen raised a concern that decoupling leaves less time to propagate attestations, effectively giving up the last 4 to 6 seconds of a slot ([01:06:09](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.or1g6gqezwuf)). Ben Edgington evaluated dumping all attestations at the beginning of a slot using network prioritization, noting that a gap remains for aggregation unless pipelining fixes it. Mikhail proposed starting aggregation in the middle of a slot with staggered publishing so earlier and later publications do not overlap and can be aggregated separately ([01:07:06](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.eypj9plupum8)). Csaba Kiraly and Sukun Tarachandani debated whether aggregation is dynamic and whether aggregators can aggregate across overlapping data, with Sukun Tarachandani asserting that aggregators cannot aggregate over overlapping aggregates without adding both, while Csaba Kiraly noted that post-quantum and zero-knowledge setups permit it ([01:08:23](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.wmd233sa7nfx)).

---

**Staggered Publishing and Sub-Committee Design**: Mikhail suggested that in the first 6 seconds, a subset of a sub-round committee votes, and in the next 6 seconds, another subset votes. Sukun Tarachandani countered that this effectively replicates the right-side design featuring multiple committees per subnet, arguing that network prioritization must be enforced or 30% of validators voting immediately will disrupt proceedings ([01:09:22](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.u05plejdk2tq)). Mikhail maintained that staggered publishing is more flexible than strict separate committees. Roberto Saltini asked whether Ben Edgington's suggestion allows flexibility between the left and right design options at deployment. Ben Edgington replied that they should punt fairness to the future and focus on delivering a 4x improvement in finality for AR ([01:11:36](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.bdxnn3a029yn)).

---

**Minimal Viable Decoupled Consensus and Finality Goals**: Sukun Tarachandani asked about a system on the right using three sub-rounds per slot to align boundaries and secure equal rewards. Ben Edgington responded that doing whatever achieves a 4x improvement in finality with minimal ambition is acceptable, recommending a minimal viable decoupled consensus that can be measured and tweaked later ([01:13:01](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.c9qnbhmzyw1d)). Roberto Saltini asked if multiple committees require prioritization to prevent penalty traffic from conflicting with goldfish or DC boots, to which Sukun Tarachandani replied that small committees might not need prioritization, whereas large ones would ([01:14:10](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.o9c04fccjjc2)). Yann Vonlanthen noted that recent devnets showed this simpler approach without fancy pipelining worked totally well. Ben Edgington joked about leaving low-hanging fruit for future job security ([01:15:55](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.7tqcvogi67ta)).

---

**Next Meeting Scheduling and Closing**: Sukun Tarachandani asked about scheduling a follow-up meeting for the following Tuesday. Yann Vonlanthen proposed dedicating the next meeting to discussing post-quantum topics, post-quantum timelines for AR, and sharing modeling work. Yann Vonlanthen apologized for the meeting ending up as a deep breakout on a single specific topic instead of high-level sharing, though Roberto Saltini noted they found the format useful. Yann Vonlanthen officially closed the session and confirmed setting up the next meeting for the following week ([01:17:17](?tab=t.7jwj1nrv6yex#heading=h.i1xbvt1fo00f)).
